decks.notes: This deck focuses on generating extra value by using cards like Paradoxical Outcome to draw cards and replay artifacts. It utilizes powerful mana rocks like Black Lotus and Moxen to accelerate its game plan, along with cards like Tolarian Academy and Mox Opal for additional mana ramp. The deck also includes key combo pieces like Time Vault and Voltaic Key to potentially win the game on the spot. It aims to efficiently control the game through countermagic like Force of Will and interaction like Swords to Plowshares, while still having the ability to quickly assemble a game-winning combo.

This deck revolves around chaining together powerful artifact spells, using cards like Paradoxical Outcome and Manifold Key to generate massive card advantage and combo off. It aims to control the board using counterspells like Force of Will and Swords to Plowshares, while also utilizing card draw and tutoring effects to find key pieces quickly. With access to powerful artifacts like Black Lotus and Moxen, the deck can generate explosive mana acceleration and overwhelm opponents with its combo potential. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion provides additional value and flexibility for the deck.

The main concept of this deck is to utilize a combination of powerful Control cards, including counterspells like Force of Will and Force of Negation, removal like Swords to Plowshares, and disruptive creatures like Lavinia, Azorius Renegade. The deck also includes card draw and graveyard interaction to maintain card advantage and disrupt opponent's strategies. The inclusion of a companion, Lurrus of the Dream-Den, adds another layer of flexibility and synergy to the deck. By controlling the board and outmaneuvering opponents, this deck aims to dominate the game and secure victory.

The deck focuses on utilizing efficient counter spells and removal to control the game, while also leveraging card advantage through cards like Ancestral Recall and Dig Through Time. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion allows for additional value from the graveyard. The deck also includes disruptive elements such as Lavinia, Azorius Renegade and Wasteland to disrupt the opponent's plans. Overall, the deck aims to out-value the opponent and disrupt their game plan while maintaining control of the game.

The deck focuses on using a combination of card advantage, disruption, and efficient removal to control the game and out-value the opponent. It utilizes powerful draw spells like Ancestral Recall and Dig Through Time, along with disruptive counterspells like Force of Will and Spell Pierce. The deck also includes removal spells like Fatal Push and Strip Mine to deal with threats. The addition of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion allows for additional value by recasting low-cost permanents from the graveyard. Overall, the deck aims to outlast opponents and win through incremental advantage.

This Dimir Control deck focuses on powerful cards and interactions to control the game and disrupt the opponent's strategies. It utilizes cards like Force of Will, Force of Negation, and Mental Misstep to counter threats, along with powerful tutors like Demonic Tutor and Vampiric Tutor to find key cards like Time Vault and Yawgmoth's Will. The deck also includes cards like Narset, Parter of Veils and Opposition Agent to disrupt the opponent's card advantage, while also utilizing powerful artifacts like Mox Sapphire and Black Lotus to ramp up mana production and cast spells quickly.

The main idea of this deck is to utilize the Dredge mechanic to fill the graveyard with key cards like Narcomoeba, Prized Amalgam, and Creeping Chill, then bring them back onto the battlefield for powerful combos. Cards like Noxious Revival and Serum Powder help with graveyard manipulation, while Force of Will and Force of Negation provide protection from disruption. Bazaar of Baghdad helps dig for combo pieces, while Hollow One and Grief provide additional threats. Overall, the goal is to overwhelm the opponent with a quick and efficient graveyard-based combo strategy.

This Vintage 1 vs 1 Esper Control deck focuses on disrupting the opponent's game plan through various forms of counter magic, removal spells, and card advantage engines. The deck utilizes powerful cards like Force of Will, Ancestral Recall, and Time Walk to control the pace of the game while also generating advantage with cards like Dig Through Time and Tamiyo, Inquisitive Student. By efficiently answering threats and maintaining card advantage, the deck aims to outvalue and outmaneuver the opponent in order to secure victory.

The main focus of this deck is to quickly fill the graveyard with key cards such as Golgari Grave-Troll, Stinkweed Imp, and Shambling Shell using cards like Bazaar of Baghdad and Serum Powder. By utilizing the Dredge mechanic, the deck aims to bring back creatures like Ichorid and Narcomoeba from the graveyard to generate significant advantage. This allows for powerful combos with cards like Prized Amalgam and Creeping Chill, while also having disruptive elements like Force of Will and Grief to protect the game plan. Additionally, the deck includes fast mana acceleration with Hollow One and potential card advantage with Silversmote Ghoul.

This deck focuses on aggressive creatures with disruptive abilities to slow down the opponent's game plan while still maintaining pressure. By playing hatebears like Anointed Peacekeeper and Chancellor of the Annex, the deck aims to disrupt the opponent's strategy by taxing their resources. Additionally, the inclusion of cards like Archon of Emeria and Cavern of Souls provide protection and make it difficult for the opponent to counter or remove key creatures. This combination of aggressive creatures and disruptive elements creates a powerful and versatile strategy.

This Esper Control deck focuses on utilizing disruption spells like Force of Will and Force of Negation to control the game, while also having access to powerful cards like Ancestral Recall and Time Walk for card advantage and extra turns. Lurrus of the Dream-Den acts as a companion, providing additional utility and value. The deck also includes hate cards like Nihil Spellbomb and Lavinia, Azorius Renegade to disrupt opponents' strategies. Overall, the deck aims to control the game through a combination of counter magic, removal, and efficient threats.

This deck focuses on a combination of efficient disruption and powerful creatures to control the game while still maintaining a fast aggressive strategy. By utilizing cards like Collector Ouphe, Deathrite Shaman, and Thoughtseize to disrupt opponents' plans, and creatures like Psychic Frog and Leovold, Emissary of Trest to apply pressure, it aims to overwhelm opponents before they can mount a defense. With the added versatility of cards like Abrupt Decay and Demonic Tutor, this deck can adapt to various situations while maintaining a proactive game plan.

This deck focuses on utilizing artifact mana acceleration and disruptive hate pieces to quickly overwhelm opponents with powerful threats. By deploying cards like Mishra's Workshop and Golos, Tireless Pilgrim, the deck aims to ramp into its threats while slowing down the opponent with cards like Thorn of Amethyst and Sphere of Resistance. The inclusion of cards like Null Rod and Crucible of Worlds further disrupt the opponent's game plan, while cards like Stonecoil Serpent and Patchwork Automaton provide aggressive threats to finish off the opponent quickly. The deck aims to land an early threat and disrupt the opponent's strategy to secure a quick victory.

The deck focuses on playing aggressive creatures while disrupting opponents with hate cards like Archon of Emeria and Chancellor of the Annex. It aims to control the game by using cards like Cavern of Souls and March of Otherworldly Light to protect its own creatures while hindering the opponent's game plan. The deck also utilizes mana acceleration with artifact mana sources such as Chrome Mox and the Moxen. Overall, the deck aims to apply pressure on the opponent while disrupting their strategy, ultimately leading to victory through a combination of aggressive creatures and disruptive hate cards.

The main concept of this Vintage 1 vs 1 Combo - Doomsday deck is to use cards like Dark Ritual, Demonic Tutor, and Doomsday to set up a winning combination of cards like Thassa's Oracle and Undercity Sewers to win the game in a single turn. The deck aims to quickly draw through the deck, find the necessary combo pieces, and win the game before the opponent can react. The deck also includes powerful cards like Ancestral Recall, Force of Will, and Time Walk to control the game and protect the combo.

The deck focuses on playing aggressively while maintaining tempo by utilizing efficient spells and powerful artifacts. By combining disruptive creatures like Lavinia and Hullbreacher with powerful spells like Force of Will and Swords to Plowshares, the deck aims to control the game while applying pressure on the opponent. The inclusion of tutoring cards like Demonic Tutor and Mystical Tutor allow for flexibility in finding key pieces like Bolas's Citadel or Ancestral Recall. The deck also benefits from fast mana sources like Black Lotus and Moxen to quickly ramp into game-winning plays.
